sourceOccurrences.label: Loop-erased law and insensitive observables
sourceOccurrences.locator: Named statement start lines in the pinned source: 22, 29, 37, 57, 70, 79, 93, 102, 111
sourceOccurrences.note: LNKT covers deterministic graph invariance, measurable loop erasure, its zero-diagonal pushforward law, and equal laws for measurable diagonal-insensitive observables or events when profiles agree off the diagonal. These statements hold for arbitrary vertex sets. EYCQ covers countable-vertex two-point probabilities, the full extended cluster-volume law and susceptibility, including infinite values. The two-vertex opposite-diagonal example and infinite complete-graph example illustrate the source witnesses. No conditioning on all loops being closed is used.

sourceOccurrences.label: Injective pullback and off-diagonal domination
sourceOccurrences.note: 1H8U preserves Countable V only, arbitrary W, off-diagonal domination and extended expectations. Pullback law identification reuses YMHY. Paths may leave the image in the larger graph, so the comparison is an inequality; countability supplies measurability on the source, not on an arbitrary target.

sourceOccurrences.label: Closed parts, independent restrictions and full-cluster laws
sourceOccurrences.note: 7CR8 is the deterministic closed-part equality; WD2J gives countable-vertex disjoint-union observables under zero cross probabilities. The general internal-restriction independence formula reuses RDX7 and needs neither zero cross probabilities nor countable ambient vertices. The symmetric second-side susceptibility/two-point formulas are extra deductions, and empty parts and diagonal coordinates are retained.

proofUses.reason: Finite all-open cylinders form a generating pi-system; uniqueness identifies the probability measure.
Injectivity makes the input coordinates of a finite output cylinder distinct, preserving its product probability.
Each output coordinate is its original value or a deterministic constant; set inclusions give the increasing-event comparison.
Independence factors all-open probabilities for intersections; complement duality and De Morgan give the union law.
A vertex bijection induces a measurable equivalence of configurations and an isomorphism of open graphs.
Injective pullback identifies the law; diagonal erasure and monotone coupling give the comparison.
A countable union excludes all cross bonds almost surely; closed-part identities and independence of the two restrictions give the component laws.
The proof uses coordinate marginals and countable unions of null events; it invokes no other wiki assertion.
